## Warm-up retrieval

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q1. In the model `lm(life_exp ~ fert_rate, data = UN_data_ch5)`, what does the *slope* coefficient represent?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>The expected `life_exp` when `fert_rate` is 0</li>
  <li>The expected change in `life_exp` for a one-unit increase in `fert_rate`</li>
  <li>The total variance in `life_exp`</li>
  <li>The correlation between the two variables</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> Slope = expected change in $y$ per one-unit change in $x$. The intercept (option a) is the predicted $y$ when $x = 0$.</div>
:::

## One numerical and one categorical explanatory variable &mdash; key idea

:::


## Check-in: One numerical and one categorical explanatory variable

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q1. In a *parallel slopes* model with one numerical and one categorical predictor:</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Each category gets its own slope and intercept</li>
  <li>Each category gets its own intercept but shares a common slope</li>
  <li>The numerical and categorical predictors are independent</li>
  <li>Only one regression line is fit</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> Parallel slopes = same slope for all groups, different intercepts per category. Distinct from interaction models, where each group also gets its own slope.</div>
:::

## Check-in: Two numerical explanatory variables

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q2. In an *interaction* model `lm(y ~ x * group)`, what does the interaction term capture?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Whether `group` predicts `y`</li>
  <li>Whether the slope of `y` on `x` differs across levels of `group`</li>
  <li>The intercept for the reference category</li>
  <li>The variance of `y`</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> Interaction terms allow the slope of `x` to vary across groups. If the interaction is large, the relationship between `x` and `y` depends on which group you're in.</div>
:::
